title: Temporal Restoration and Spatial Rewiring for Source-Free Multivariate Time Series Domain Adaptation

problem.claim: Source-free domain adaptation must adapt a pretrained model to an unlabeled target domain without accessing source data.

gap.claim: Existing source-free domain adaptation methods struggle on multivariate time series because they do not account for intrinsic spatial correlations that help preserve invariant cross-domain information.

contributions.claim: TERSE is a source-free domain adaptation method for multivariate time series that combines a customized spatial-temporal feature encoder with temporal restoration and spatial rewiring tasks.
During target adaptation, TERSE guides the target encoder toward spatially and temporally consistent features using source-pretrained restoration and rewiring networks.
TERSE is presented as a plug-and-play module that can be integrated into established source-free domain adaptation methods.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe TERSE as the first approach to simultaneously consider spatial-temporal consistency in multivariate time-series source-free domain adaptation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on three real-world time-series datasets are reported to demonstrate the effectiveness and versatility of TERSE.
The authors report that TERSE can model and transfer spatial-temporal dependencies across domains to facilitate implicit feature alignment.

narrative_sequence.summary: Source-free domain adaptation operates without access to source data while adapting to an unlabeled target domain.
Existing methods underperform on multivariate time series because they overlook intrinsic spatial correlations and their role in invariant information.
TERSE addresses the gap with spatial-temporal encoding, temporal restoration, and spatial rewiring.
Source-pretrained restoration and rewiring networks guide spatially and temporally consistent target features, enabling implicit feature alignment.
The authors report effectiveness and versatility on three real-world datasets and describe the method as plug-and-play.

source_observation.claim: The method uses temporal restoration and spatial rewiring tasks to reconstruct masked temporal content and correlated spatial structures.

interpretation.claim: For multivariate time-series adaptation, preserving both temporal structure and cross-variable relationships may provide complementary self-supervision.

application.claim: A related adaptation design could pair temporal reconstruction objectives with objectives that restore or model masked inter-variable structures.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this combination benefits datasets whose variables lack meaningful spatial or cross-variable correlations.

unknowns: The three datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not specified.
The source and target domains and adaptation protocol are not specified.
Ablation results and computational or memory costs are not specified.
The abstract does not provide limitations or failure cases.
